title: Simultaneous normal constants and compatible finite product groups
statement:
Let $e$ be a field, $I$ a nonempty finite set, and, for each $i\in I$, let $F_i/e$ be a finite field extension and $J_i$ a finite group equipped with a homomorphism $\rho_i:J_i\to\operatorname{Aut}_e(F_i)$. The homomorphisms need not be injective. There exist a finite normal extension $K/e$ and $e$-embeddings $u_i:F_i\hookrightarrow K$ with the following properties. Put $A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$, $G=A\times\prod_{t\in I}J_t$, and let $\pi:G\to A$ be the first projection. The groups $A$ and $G$ are finite and $\pi$ is surjective. For each $i$, the subset
$$\Gamma_i=\{(a,(j_t)_t)\in G: a\circ u_i=u_i\circ\rho_i(j_i)\}$$
is a subgroup, and its coordinate map $r_i:\Gamma_i\to J_i$ is surjective. Moreover
$$\pi(\ker r_i)=\operatorname{Aut}_{u_i(F_i)}(K)$$
as subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$: an automorphism on the right fixes every element of the embedded field $u_i(F_i)$. The fixed subfield $K^{\pi(G)}=\{x\in K: a(x)=x\text{ for every }a\in\pi(G)\}$ is purely inseparable over $e$. Here normal means that the minimal polynomial over $e$ of every element of $K$ splits into linear factors in $K[T]$; no separability of $F_i/e$ or $K/e$ is assumed. Fields, finite extensions, and pure inseparability use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], and [def-pc-field-tower].

proof.text: Enumerate $I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_n\}$. Inductively construct a finite $L_r/e$ with embeddings of $F_{i_1},\ldots,F_{i_r}$, starting with $L_0=e$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], embed $L_r$ and $F_{i_{r+1}}$ over $e$ into a field $\Omega_r$. Identify both fields with their images in $\Omega_r$; the images of $e$ agree because the embeddings fix $e$. Take their compositum $L_{r+1}$ in $\Omega_r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound], $L_{r+1}/L_r$ is finite with degree at most $[F_{i_{r+1}}:e]$. It is finite over $e$ directly: if $b_s$ span $L_r/e$ and $c_t$ span $L_{r+1}/L_r$, then writing $x=\sum_t a_tc_t$ and $a_t=\sum_s d_{st}b_s$ expresses $x$ as an $e$-linear combination of the finitely many $b_sc_t$. Compose the old embeddings with the induced embedding $L_r\hookrightarrow L_{r+1}$ and use the new embedding of $F_{i_{r+1}}$. This proves the induction and supplies $L_n$.

source.place: Tags 0H7K (lemma-common-extension-field), 09ID (definition-compositum); compositum finiteness as in the cited degree-bound node; finite-family induction and spanning-set argument written by Q120.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension] to the finite extension $L_n/e$. It gives an extension $K/L_n$ finite and normal over $e$. Composing the embeddings into $L_n$ with $L_n\hookrightarrow K$ gives all $u_i$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-finitely-many-embeddings], applied with base $e$, domain $K$ and codomain $K$, the set of $e$-algebra maps $K\to K$ is finite. Forgetting the inverse embeds $A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$ in this set, so $A$ is finite. Thus $G=A\times\prod_{t\in I}J_t$ is finite. The map $a\mapsto(a,(1)_t)$ is a right inverse of $\pi$, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 09HS (lemma-normal-and-automorphisms); use the existing more general embedding-count node; finite products and the displayed section are elementary.

proof.text: Fix $i$. The identity belongs to $\Gamma_i$. If $(a,j),(b,k)\in\Gamma_i$, then $ab\circ u_i=a\circ u_i\circ\rho_i(k_i)=u_i\circ\rho_i(j_i)\circ\rho_i(k_i)=u_i\circ\rho_i(j_ik_i)$, so their product belongs to $\Gamma_i$. From $a\circ u_i=u_i\circ\rho_i(j_i)$, composing on the left with $a^{-1}$ and on the right with $\rho_i(j_i)^{-1}$ gives $a^{-1}\circ u_i=u_i\circ\rho_i(j_i^{-1})$. Thus inverses belong as well. This proves the subgroup assertion, and restriction of the $i$th coordinate projection is the homomorphism $r_i$.

source.place: ILO X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, graph enlargement before (2.b); elementary product-group calculation written by Q120.

proof.text: Given $j\in J_i$, conjugate $\rho_i(j)$ by $u_i$ to obtain an $e$-automorphism $\tau$ of the subfield $u_i(F_i)\subseteq K$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-intermediate-isomorphism-lifts] with $k=e$, $L=K$ and $M_1=M_2=u_i(F_i)$. It gives $a\in A$ satisfying $a\circ u_i=u_i\circ\rho_i(j)$. Take $j_i=j$ and $j_t=1$ for $t\ne i$. Then $(a,(j_t)_t)\in\Gamma_i$ and maps to $j$, proving $r_i$ surjective.

source.place: Tag 0BME (lemma-lift-maps), part (2); apply to the embedded intermediate field, with no normality assumption on it.

proof.text: If $(a,(j_t)_t)\in\ker r_i$, then $j_i=1$ and its compatibility equation reads $a\circ u_i=u_i$, so $a$ fixes $u_i(F_i)$ pointwise. This gives $\pi(\ker r_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_{u_i(F_i)}(K)$. Conversely, if $a\in A$ fixes $u_i(F_i)$, the tuple $(a,(1)_t)$ belongs to $\Gamma_i$ and to $\ker r_i$, and projects to $a$. This gives the reverse inclusion and hence the asserted subgroup equality.

source.place: ILO X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, graph enlargement; elementary kernel-image calculation for the compatible product subgroups, written by Q120.

proof.text: Since $\pi$ is surjective, its image is $A$ and $K^{\pi(G)}=K^A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-fixed-field-purely-inseparable] to $K/e$, which is algebraic and normal by step 2. It says exactly that $K^A/e$ is purely inseparable, as required.
